purpose: Screen genuine moving-lane conversions for a new empirical analysis of flow and time, beyond the Brooklyn Bridge pandemic case.
scoring: Ordinal data-readiness score 0-4, not causal validity or probability: 0=wrong intervention; 1=historical descriptive evidence only; 2=usable counts/time but alignment or counterfactual missing; 3=run-level outcome plus contemporaneous comparison observations, still important identification problems; 4=aligned multimode repeated pre/post outcomes with defensible controls. No investigated candidate scored4.

candidates.treatment: Three moving lanes to two, June2010; bike path, signal retiming, islands and loading changes. Separate June27 B69 rerouting also changes this corridor and two comparison streets.
candidates.obtained: DOT67-page summary and underlying data;416 travel-time runs extracted,384 weekday runs in four corridors over two before and two after weekdays. Reproduce.py and tidyCSV provided in ppw/.
candidates.exact_tables: PDF p51 route/period summary; pp52-59 individual runs; p40 dated motor peak counts; pp41-46 hourly motor tables; pp5/16 bicycle aggregate observations; pp47-48 combined-mode display uses unmatched dates/locations.
candidates.dates: Travel time May11-12,2010 versusOct19-20,2010; bicycleJun9,2009 versusAug17,Sep15,Oct12,Nov9,2010 weekdays; motorApr2009/May2010 versusOct2010.
candidates.controls: 6thNB,7thSB,8thNB same surveyed days and half-hour schedule. 7th/8th directly affected by B69 relocation; 6th opposite direction and susceptible to diversion. Only one pre wave prevents a parallel-trend test.
candidates.result: PPW mean driving time change-7.125sec; controlled daily change ranges-35.833 to+10.917sec across individual controls. Hypothetical equal25drives on each corridor changes+0.920vehicle-minutes per100drives. No causal confidence interval or observed all-person total.
candidates.remaining_gap: No aligned all-person flow, repeated-pre time waves, or uncontaminated direction-matched control. Study estimates street/bus-change package context, not bike-lane-only effect.

candidates.treatment: Moving lanes removed for protected bike facilities and bus priority; M15 SBS launchedOct10,2010.
candidates.obtained: 2011 M15 progress report and September2011 CB8 presentation downloaded in first-second/.
candidates.exact_tables: Progress report PDF p21 Figures14/15 vehicle volumes at five intersections per avenue; p22 Figure10 bicycle counts; p20 taxi speed diagrams. SeptemberCB8 presentation p4 motor volumes; p7 bicycle counts.
candidates.dates: MotorJune2009 versusApril2011; taxiNovember2009 versusNovember2010; bicycle2010 versus2011 seasonal averages (body saysApril-October, tableApril-September).
candidates.controls: Upstream avenue segments have different bus/bike treatments and SecondAvenueSubway works. No untreated comparison raw travel-time panel located.
candidates.remaining_gap: Different dates/geographies and bundled SBS/fare/signal changes. Public taxi trip endpoints alone cannot reproduce DOT's80%-on-route GPS restriction.

candidates.treatment: Four unassigned moving lanes to three through lanes, initially16th-23rdStreet fall2007;23rd-31st extension2008.
candidates.obtained: DOTSeptember2014report downloaded;pp20-21 explicitly identify lane removal. NACTO project description verifies geometry. Original2008DOT report link currently404.
candidates.controls: Economic reports have comparison corridors, but these are sales controls, not verified traffic-flow or travel-time panels.
candidates.remaining_gap: No acquired aligned raw motor/bicycle pre/post with credible control. Sales-control evidence does not fill that gap.

candidates.treatment: One southbound car lane becomes protected two-way bikeway. Construction documented by September2015; a prior plan scheduled April2015 start. OpeningApril29,2016; later punch-list work. Exact temporary and permanent lane-closure dates not verified. Existing three Brooklyn-bound lanes already merged to two at McGuinness/Green Street, so lane removal does not by itself establish lost bottleneck capacity.
candidates.obtained: Opening press release and2016bridge report; sensor metadata downloaded. Pulaski automated bicycle series startsJune24,2017, after treatment. Companion analyst obtained2014-18 hourly McGuinness motor data, an approach corridor rather than bridge screenline.
candidates.dates: Manual bike/pedestrian countsApril2009 andApril2013 are bothpre. Automatedbikefirstdata2017-06-24. MotorATR2016postsample includesJuly4holiday; construction should not be coded asfullyuntreated.
candidates.controls: Potential NYSDOTcontinuous motor stations require separate availability/pretrend checks; no matched pre2016automatic bicycle outcome.
candidates.remaining_gap: Approach motor flows cannot be added to bridge bicycle counts. No continuous pre-bike series, exact lane-closure event, or bus-occupancy series verified.

candidates.reason_excluded: Officialproject page and2014reportp26 explicitly say no lane removal; existing moving lanes retained and narrowed.
candidates.obtained: 2011assessment and2012postimplementation PDFs downloaded in columbus/;2012p7 gives AM/PM bicycles111→127/200→236 and motor3250→2948/2847→2739, but different dates and cross-sections.
